MRI of left Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Ax T2 FS, Cor T2 FS

> Multifocal wearing of articular cartilage of left knee, more severe at femoral trochlea ( grade 4 chondromalacia) and medial femoral condyle (grade 3-4 chondromalacia) and posterior medial plateau and some spur formation, reflecting osteoarthritis.
  Mild fraying articular cartilage of lateral femorotibial joint, reflecting grade 2 chondromalacia of lateral femoral conydle and grade 2-3 chondromalacia of posterior lateral tibial plateau.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
   A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst.
> Irregular contour of tibial tuberosity with some bony fragmentations (srs: [ID].
   Thickening of patellar tendon with increased interstitial signal inside and some laxity fibers on F/S T2WI, in favor of tendinosis with partial tear.
> Mild laxity of ACL with increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of mucoid degeneration.
> P medial & lateral collateral ligaments and PCL appear to be within normal.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration.
> Slight thickening and interstitial increased signal intensity of iliotibial band on F/S T2WI, in favor of tendinosis.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee with grade 3-4 chondromalacia, more prominent at medial compartement and patellofemoral joint but no significant subchondral edema or cystic change over left knee; [DATE].
2. Old Osgood-Schlatter disease of left knee; [DATE].
3. Degeneration of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
5. Synovitis of left knee with suprapatellar bursitis and Baker's cyst ; patellar plicae.
6. Degeneration of ACL and iliotibial band.

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and physical examination

Findings:  There is a minor knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild - moderate osteophyte formation in the medial and lateral compartment. Minor fraying of the medial compartment articular cartilage is noted but no cartilage loss.  Moderate - severe patellofemoral dysplasia is noted. The patella lies in a lateralized position. T T T G distance is normal. There is severe loss of the lateral patellofemoral articular cartilage with underlying bony change.  
Conclusion: Patellar maltracking with severe lateral patellofemoral degeneration.

There is an undisplaced, extensive degenerative tear through the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, displaying both radial as well as horizontal components, with early medial extrusion at the level of the body, together with an overlying grade 1 superficial MCL sprain.
There are no accompanying displaced meniscal fragments.

Intact lateral meniscus, cruciate and lateral collateral ligaments, distal iliotibial band, extensor tendons and the popliteus musculotendinous unit.
No fracture or marrow infiltration.

Minor articular cartilage fraying noted in the more central aspect of the middle third of the medial femoral condyle.
Mild, focal lateral retropatellar chondral damage is also present.
Well-maintained remaining tricompartmental hyaline articular cartilage surfaces.

Tiny suprapatellar effusion, there are no intra-articular bodies.
Grossly unremarkable imaged extra-articular soft tissues, save for a small, lobulated non ruptured Baker's cyst.

Findings:  Small joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular loose bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments.  Complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus, extending to the root with a prominent radial oblique component. Intact lateral meniscus.  Normal appearance of the distal biceps femoris tendon, distal iliotibial band, popliteus tendon and pes anserine tendons. Intact quadriceps and patellar tendons. No evidence of fat pad impingement.  Severe patellofemoral degenerative change with full-thickness chondral loss and underlying bone changes along the lateral retropatellar facet and corresponding femoral trochlea surface, together with marginal osteophyte formation. Focal full-thickness chondral loss in the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle with underlying bone stress changes. Relatively well-maintained lateral tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage. Marginal osteophyte formation is also noted in the tibiofemoral compartments.  
Conclusion:  Complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus, extending to the root with a prominent radial oblique component. Severe patellofemoral and to lesser extent medial tibiofemoral compartment degenerative changes.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: History of knee pain status post fall.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovial proliferation. Partial sprain of the posterior joint capsule. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate, ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness fissuring medial patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Mild mucoid degeneration, otherwise intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Grade 2 midsubstance sprain of the PCL characterized by periligamentous edema and partial fiber disruption.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Subcutaneous soft tissue edema about the anteromedial knee compatible with underlying soft tissue contusion. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Grade 2 midsubstance PCL sprain.
2.	Subcutaneous soft tissue contusion anteromedial knee.
3.	Moderate joint effusion with synovitis and partial disruption of the posterior joint capsule.
4.	Moderate ruptured Baker's cyst.
